before.exampleAnswer: Values from 20 through 40, including both ends

after.exampleAnswer: BETWEEN includes both endpoints, so 20 and 40 pass as well as values between them. An unknown amount does not pass this comparison.
Use amount IS NULL to test for a missing value. Equality to NULL does not evaluate to true in SQL.
ORDER BY id ASC explicitly requests increasing ids. Without ORDER BY, the query makes no promise about the order of its result rows.
WHERE first keeps paid rows, ORDER BY amount ASC puts the smallest amounts first, and LIMIT 2 keeps the first two. id provides a stable order for ties.

before.exampleAnswer: Add a unique id as a tie-breaker

after.exampleAnswer: Add a unique id after amount in ORDER BY. It settles ties on amount so the same rows have a defined order.
DISTINCT compares the complete selected row. Even when item repeats, the unique id makes every item-and-id pair different.
DISTINCT removes duplicate selected rows from the query result. It does not delete rows from the stored table.
SQLite SUM(amount) returns NULL when there are no non-NULL input values, including an empty matching set. COUNT instead returns zero for an empty set.
COALESCE replaces each missing amount with zero before averaging. Those rows now contribute to the denominator, which can change the average.
HAVING filters groups after aggregation, so it can test SUM(amount). WHERE filters the input rows before their group totals are computed.

before.exampleAnswer: It filters individual rows before grouping

after.exampleAnswer: WHERE retains only paid input rows before grouping. Group counts and totals are calculated from that filtered set.
An INNER JOIN retains only matching pairs. Dee has no matching order in this dataset, so her customer row contributes no result row.
c.id = o.customer_id follows the customer reference stored on each order. Matching the two tables' unrelated id columns would connect the wrong records.

after.exampleAnswer: EXISTS asks whether any matching order exists for each outer customer row. It does not create one outer row per match, so Ada appears once.
A correlated subquery uses a value from the current outer row. Its meaning depends on which outer row is being considered.
UNION stacks compatible rows from its SELECT results and removes duplicates. It combines rows vertically rather than matching columns through a join.

before.exampleAnswer: They must have the same number of result columns

after.exampleAnswer: Each SELECT must return the same number of columns, with corresponding columns representing compatible values. UNION aligns columns by position, not by name.
A window calculation adds a result to each retained order row. Unlike GROUP BY aggregation, it does not collapse the rows into one row per group.

before.exampleAnswer: The two rows no longer tie

after.exampleAnswer: Window ties depend on every ORDER BY expression. Adding distinct ids makes the two 80 rows different ordering keys, so they no longer tie.
ROW_NUMBER assigns a separate consecutive position to every row in the window's specified order. A unique tie-breaker makes that order deterministic.

before.exampleAnswer: Use an outer query over the numbered result

after.exampleAnswer: Compute ROW_NUMBER in an inner query or CTE, then filter position = 1 in the outer query. SQLite cannot use that window result in the same SELECT's WHERE clause.

before.exampleAnswer: Which rows belong to each calculation window

after.exampleAnswer: PARTITION BY splits the rows into separate windows for the calculation. It changes which rows are compared or accumulated together without itself collapsing them.
